name: codeterm
about: CodeTerm CLI — control your terminal multiplexer

args.name: json
args.help: Output raw JSON instead of human-readable text

args.name: mesh
args.help: Execute command on a remote mesh peer instead of locally

subcommands.name: agent
subcommands.about: Agent hierarchy management

subcommands.name: allow-spawn
subcommands.about: Toggle whether a pane can spawn children

subcommands.name: compact
subcommands.about: Compact agent context (sends /compact to Claude)

subcommands.name: link
subcommands.about: Link a pane as worker under a parent

args.name: pane
args.help: Pane ID to link (default: current focused pane)

subcommands.name: model
subcommands.about: Switch agent model. Claude only — Codex /model is an interactive picker, respawn with `agent spawn codex --model X` instead

args.name: name
args.help: Model name (Claude: sonnet, haiku, opus). Run `agent models claude` to list

subcommands.name: models
subcommands.about: List available models for a specific provider

subcommands.name: providers
subcommands.about: List available agent providers (claude, codex, ...) with their display names, default models, and capability flags

subcommands.name: report
subcommands.about: Send a report to your parent in the hierarchy

subcommands.name: reports
subcommands.about: Read reports (for orchestrator panes)

args.name: limit
args.help: Show only the N most recent reports (default: all)

subcommands.name: restart
subcommands.about: Restart agent (gracefully /exit + auto-resume to pick up settings or recover)

args.name: force
args.help: Skip the graceful exit and force-kill instead. Use only when the agent is hung

args.name: grace_secs
args.help: Wait this long for graceful exit before force-killing (seconds)

subcommands.name: set-orchestrator
subcommands.about: Mark a pane as orchestrator (top-level, can spawn workers)

subcommands.name: spawn
subcommands.about: Spawn a new agent (creates tab in workspace, linked in hierarchy)

args.name: agent
args.help: Agent provider id. Run `codeterm agent providers` to list registered providers (e.g. claude, codex, opencode). Default: claude

args.name: model
args.help: Model selector (e.g. "github-copilot/claude-haiku-4.5", "gpt-5"). The provider knows whether to emit `-m X` or `--model X` — caller passes the model string opaque. Run `codeterm agent models <provider>` to see what's available

args.name: task
args.help: Task to send after agent starts

args.name: workspace
args.help: Target workspace ID (default: parent's workspace or active workspace)

subcommands.name: unlink
subcommands.about: Remove a pane's role (also orphans children)

subcommands.name: bridge
subcommands.about: Send a message to an external service (Telegram, etc.)

subcommands.name: migrate
subcommands.about: Migrate active bridge poller from this node to another mesh peer

args.name: announce
args.help: Send a one-shot "now serving from <host>" message to the sentinel chat

args.name: announce_chat_id
args.help: Sentinel chat id for --announce. Defaults to the maintainer's chat

args.name: claim_timeout_ms
args.help: How long target may take to claim the Telegram lock before the migration is considered failed (ms)

args.name: force
args.help: Skip preflight target-state check (for force migrations)

args.name: no_rollback
args.help: Skip auto-rollback if target claim fails (leave source disabled)

args.name: to
args.help: Target peer instance_name (as shown in `codeterm mesh peers`)

subcommands.name: react
subcommands.about: Set an emoji reaction on a message

subcommands.name: restart
subcommands.about: Start or restart messaging bridge (Telegram, etc.)

subcommands.name: send
subcommands.about: Send a message to Telegram or other service

args.name: append
args.help: Append to previous message instead of replacing (edits existing message)

args.name: caption
args.help: Caption for media (alternative to positional text)

args.name: text
args.help: Message text (also used as caption for media types)

args.name: type
args.help: Content type: text, photo, document, voice, animation, video, sticker

subcommands.name: capabilities
subcommands.about: List all available API methods

subcommands.name: cli-manifest
subcommands.about: Dump the CLI command tree as JSON (source of truth for docs/prompts/cards)

subcommands.name: config
subcommands.about: Read or write CodeTerm configuration

subcommands.name: get
subcommands.about: Get a config value (dot-notation, e.g. "integrations.telegram_enabled")

subcommands.name: set
subcommands.about: Set a config value (JSON-compatible: true, false, 42, "string")

subcommands.name: cron
subcommands.about: Cron job management

subcommands.name: cancel
subcommands.about: Stop any currently-running executions of a cron job without deleting the job definition. Future scheduled fires still run

subcommands.name: complete
subcommands.about: Mark a cron run as complete (called by agent at end of task)

subcommands.name: create
subcommands.about: Create a cron job

args.name: creator_pane
args.help: Pane ID to receive reports from cron agent (default: $CODETERM_PANE_ID)

args.name: jitter_max_ms
args.help: Max jitter in milliseconds added to each scheduled fire. 0 = off. Omit for default (10% of interval, clamped to [1m, 30m])

args.name: model
args.help: Model within the agent provider (e.g. "opus", "haiku", "gpt-5.4-mini"). Leave unset to use the provider default

args.name: once
args.help: Oneshot: fire once at scheduled time, then auto-delete

args.name: schedule
args.help: Cron schedule (5-field: "*/30 * * * *") or oneshot time ("in 5m", ISO8601)

args.name: timeout_secs
args.help: Per-cron run timeout (seconds). Overrides global memory.worker_timeout_seconds. Set high (e.g. 1800) for long-running tasks like memory dreaming

args.name: tz
args.help: IANA timezone for the schedule (e.g. "Europe/Riga"). Default: UTC

subcommands.name: delete
subcommands.about: Delete a cron job

subcommands.name: disable
subcommands.about: Disable a cron job

subcommands.name: edit
subcommands.about: Edit a cron job

args.name: jitter_max_ms
args.help: Max jitter in milliseconds added to each scheduled fire. Set 0 to disable jitter. Omit to leave unchanged

args.name: model
args.help: Model within the agent provider. Pass empty string to clear

args.name: timeout_secs
args.help: Per-cron run timeout (seconds). 0 clears the override (back to global default)

args.name: tz
args.help: IANA timezone (e.g. "Europe/Riga"). Pass empty string to clear back to UTC

subcommands.name: enable
subcommands.about: Enable a cron job

subcommands.name: history
subcommands.about: Show run history

subcommands.name: list
subcommands.about: List cron jobs

subcommands.name: trigger
subcommands.about: Manually trigger a cron job now

subcommands.name: debug
subcommands.about: Internal diagnostics — verify crash reporter, etc. Dev-only; hidden from --help because the matching daemon endpoint is gated to debug builds. Calling against a prod daemon returns Method-not-found

subcommands.name: crash
subcommands.about: Trigger a synthetic crash to verify the crash-reporter writes files. Daemon dies (segv/abort) or just records a panic report (panic). Only available in dev builds

subcommands.name: docs
subcommands.about: Read embedded CodeTerm documentation. Docs are bundled into the CLI binary at compile time so agents can request them on demand without bloating the system prompt. `codeterm docs` lists, `codeterm docs <name>` prints a bounded preview inside CodeTerm panes; pass --full for the complete doc. Names are case-insensitive and match the .md stem (CONFIG, API, MESH, MEMORY, BUILD, PROMPTS, SKILLS, TESTING)

args.name: full
args.help: Print the complete document even inside a CodeTerm pane

args.name: name
args.help: Doc name (e.g. CONFIG, API, MESH). Omit to list all available docs

subcommands.name: get-output
subcommands.about: Get terminal output from a pane (default: current pane)

args.name: lines
args.help: Maximum number of lines to return (approximate)

args.name: pane
args.help: Target pane ID (default: $CODETERM_PANE_ID or focused pane)

subcommands.name: identify
subcommands.about: Show CodeTerm version and system info

subcommands.name: keepawake
subcommands.about: Prevent the system from sleeping while an agent is running

subcommands.name: start
subcommands.about: Start keeping the system awake

subcommands.name: status
subcommands.about: Show current keep-awake status (default)

subcommands.name: stop
subcommands.about: Stop the current keep-awake session

subcommands.name: mem
subcommands.about: Unified memory store — skills, facts, notes, scripts, peers, preferences

subcommands.name: calibration
subcommands.about: Memory calibration: review or trigger the dreamer's importance/archive sweep

subcommands.name: log
subcommands.about: Show recent calibration changes (audit log)

subcommands.name: sweep
subcommands.about: Manually trigger a calibration sweep (Sunday only unless --force)

args.name: force
args.help: Bypass the day-of-week gate. Manual / testing

subcommands.name: delete
subcommands.about: Delete an item by id

subcommands.name: dream
subcommands.about: Dreamer review/apply: run a daemon-routed dream phase, or apply a reviewed re-cluster plan against the local mem DB

subcommands.name: apply
subcommands.about: Re-parse a plan file and call `introduce_topic` for each YAML-fenced action block. Malformed individual fences become warnings; the rest still run. After a successful run the file is renamed to `<name>-applied.md` with a summary footer appended. Plans are hand-written or produced by a future Dreamer re-cluster phase

args.name: plan_file
args.help: Path to the plan markdown file

subcommands.name: diary
subcommands.about: Show the most recent dream diary entries (the structured PATTERN / CONNECTION / IDEA / WHAT IF / HUBS / ONE ACTION reflections the REM agent writes after each dream cycle). Use this to read the Dreamer's fresh observations before acting on them

args.name: limit
args.help: How many entries to return (most-recent first)

subcommands.name: run
subcommands.about: Run dreaming consolidation via the daemon. Phases: light, deep, normalize, all (default). Replaces the v1.1.22 `mem dream --phase ...` form which is gone in v1.1.23

args.name: phase
args.help: Which phase to run: light | deep | normalize | all

subcommands.name: extract-pending
subcommands.about: Re-run extraction workers for items that haven't been extracted yet. Useful after LLM API failures, quota resets, or bulk imports with skip_extract. Workers fire sequentially with a short delay

args.name: limit
args.help: Maximum number of items to queue (default 200)

subcommands.name: flush
subcommands.about: Flush a pane's PTY scrollback as a kind=conversation mem_item (called by PreCompact hook before context summarization)

subcommands.name: forget
subcommands.about: Batch-delete every item in an area (use sparingly)

subcommands.name: get
subcommands.about: Print one item by id

subcommands.name: graph
subcommands.about: Graph operations

subcommands.name: alias
subcommands.about: Merge one entity into another (alias → canonical)

subcommands.name: augment-entity
subcommands.about: Patch properties on an existing entity (audit-logged)

args.name: patch
args.help: JSON object of properties to merge in (e.g. '{"city":"Riga"}')

subcommands.name: create
subcommands.about: Create a graph entity

subcommands.name: delete-entity
subcommands.about: Delete an entity by id (audited). Refuses if it has active relations unless --force, in which case those relations are cascade-deleted too

args.name: force
args.help: Cascade-delete active relations referencing this entity

args.name: purge_history
args.help: Also hard-delete invalidated (historical) relations referencing this entity. Default false: history is preserved as ghost rows for `revive-broken` and timeline queries. Set this when you're sure the entity is gone for good

subcommands.name: delete-relations
subcommands.about: Delete relations by explicit rowids (audited to graph_purge_log)

subcommands.name: find-duplicate-entities
subcommands.about: Find duplicate entities (exact name match, alias chain, or vector similarity)

args.name: entity_type
args.help: Restrict `vector` strategy to entities of this type (Person, Tech, Project, ...)

args.name: threshold
args.help: Cosine similarity threshold for `vector` strategy (0.0-1.0). 0.90+ = strong-merge candidate, 0.85+ = review-worthy

subcommands.name: find-duplicate-relations
subcommands.about: Find duplicate relations grouped by selected columns. Read-only diagnostic — does not mutate the graph

args.name: group_by
args.help: Comma-separated columns from: from_id,relation_type,to_id,scope,valid_from. Default excludes valid_from because the relations UNIQUE(from,rel,to,valid_from) makes grouping by all four a guaranteed no-op — meaningful dedup is on the triple

subcommands.name: get
subcommands.about: Inspect a graph entity: properties_json + degree summary. Filling the gap that mem search only hits mem_items, not entities. Use this when you need email/phone/role/whatever a Person/Tech/Project entity carries in its properties — `mem graph related` returns relations only

subcommands.name: hubs
subcommands.about: List hub nodes — entities with active degree at or above threshold. Each hub returns its degree, the relation_type distribution, and a sample of neighbors with titles. Used by the Dreamer recluster phase to decide which hubs to decompose into topic_* intermediates

subcommands.name: introduce-topic
subcommands.about: Atomically introduce a topic intermediate: insert topic entity (if missing), link sources → topic → anchor, invalidate direct sources → anchor edges

args.name: sources
args.help: Comma-separated source ids (s1,s2,s3) OR @path/to/file (one per line; '#'-prefixed and blank lines ignored)

subcommands.name: invalidate
subcommands.about: Invalidate a relation (set valid_to, preserve history)

subcommands.name: islands
subcommands.about: List connected components of size <= max-size — disconnected "islands" the Dreamer should bridge or delete. Returns component member id/kind/title/area, plus a `suggested_anchor` derived from shared area / kind / title-keywords across members. JSON mode emits JSONL (one component per line, sorted by size asc)

args.name: limit
args.help: Maximum number of components to emit (caps verbose output)

args.name: max_size
args.help: Maximum component size to include (default 6 — pairs through small clusters; bigger groups are real sub-graphs)

subcommands.name: merge-relations
subcommands.about: Merge relations into `keep`, folding properties/confidence

args.name: keep
args.help: Rowid of the relation to keep (its properties and rowid survive)

args.name: merge
args.help: Comma-separated rowids to fold into `keep` (these are deleted)

subcommands.name: orphans
subcommands.about: List nodes with degree 0 — true orphans (entities with no relations, mem_items not pointed at by anything). Output: id, kind, title, area, last access. JSON mode emits a flat array

args.name: limit
args.help: Cap the number of orphans emitted

subcommands.name: path
subcommands.about: Shortest path between two entities

args.name: include_invalidated
args.help: Include relations whose valid_to is set (default: active-only)

subcommands.name: purge-invalidated
subcommands.about: Hard-delete relations whose valid_to is set. Optional filters by cutoff date and reason substring. Audited to graph_purge_log

args.name: before
args.help: Only purge rows with valid_to before this RFC 3339 timestamp

args.name: dry_run
args.help: Print count without modifying any rows or writing audit row

subcommands.name: relate
subcommands.about: Create a relation between entities or mem_items

args.name: reason
args.help: Free-text reason; written to relations.reason for audit

subcommands.name: related
subcommands.about: List outgoing relations from an id

args.name: include_invalidated
args.help: Include relations whose valid_to is set (default: active-only)

subcommands.name: repair-orphan-blobs
subcommands.about: Find and (optionally) delete sha256_*.txt blob files in the mem blobs directory that no mem_item references. CAS-aware sweep (refcount = 0)

subcommands.name: repair-orphan-vectors
subcommands.about: Find and (optionally) delete orphan rows in mem_vectors — vectors whose mem_id has no matching mem_items / entities row. One-shot legacy cleanup

subcommands.name: revive-broken
subcommands.about: Restore valid_to=NULL for relations whose endpoints both still exist in entities or mem_items. Idempotent

subcommands.name: route
subcommands.about: Atomically re-route an active direct edge (from → to) through an intermediate (from → via → to). Invalidates the original direct edge

args.name: rel_in
args.help: Relation type for the from→via segment (default = original rel)

args.name: rel_out
args.help: Relation type for the via→to segment (default = original rel)

subcommands.name: timeline
subcommands.about: Full temporal timeline for an entity

args.name: include_invalidated
args.help: Include relations whose valid_to is set (default: active-only)

subcommands.name: traverse
subcommands.about: BFS traversal from an entity (max_hops cap)

args.name: include_invalidated
args.help: Include relations whose valid_to is set (default: active-only)

subcommands.name: tunnels
subcommands.about: List entities bridging 2+ areas (cross-project connections)

args.name: include_invalidated
args.help: Include relations whose valid_to is set (default: active-only)

subcommands.name: history
subcommands.about: Print the full audit trail for one item (create/update/promote/delete)

subcommands.name: learn
subcommands.about: Capture a quick learning (insight, error, feature request)

args.name: text
args.help: What you learned. If omitted and stdin piped, read stdin

subcommands.name: learn-list
subcommands.about: List pending learnings (kind=learning items)

subcommands.name: learn-promote
subcommands.about: Promote a learning to a fact (raises importance)

subcommands.name: pin
subcommands.about: Pin a mem item so it always loads in L1 wake-up

subcommands.name: pinned
subcommands.about: List all currently pinned items, ordered by importance/evidence/recency

subcommands.name: reembed
subcommands.about: Re-embed mem_items and/or graph entities into mem_vectors. Use this after swapping the embedder model, or to backfill existing entities that pre-date the auto-embed-on-create wiring. Daemon-routed (the daemon owns the embedder process). Idempotent

args.name: scope
args.help: What to re-embed: items (mem_items) | entities (graph) | all

subcommands.name: run-worker
subcommands.about: Run a single mem maintenance pass in this subprocess. Opens the DB directly (multi-process WAL) and performs one phase of work, then exits. Used by the daemon's supervisor so a panic / OOM in dreaming or librarian cannot take the API down

args.name: db_path
args.help: Override the path to knowledge.db. Defaults to the same data dir the CLI uses elsewhere (`~/.codeterm/mem/knowledge.db` for prod, `~/.codeterm-dev/mem/knowledge.db` for dev)

args.name: kind
args.help: Which phase to run: dreaming-light | dreaming-deep | dreaming-normalize | librarian-once

subcommands.name: save
subcommands.about: Save a new mem item

args.name: body
args.help: Body content. If omitted and stdin is piped, read stdin

args.name: importance
args.help: Importance 1-5 (default 3.0). Higher = more likely in L1 wake-up

args.name: kind
args.help: Item kind: skill | fact | note | conversation | script | peer | preference | daily | learning | rule | summary

args.name: pin
args.help: Pin the item for L1 wake-up (always loaded)

args.name: replace
args.help: Overwrite an existing row with the same id (upsert). Use this to update the bundled identity placeholder or any pinned record

args.name: skip_extract
args.help: Skip auto-extraction worker for this save

args.name: source_path
args.help: Path to source file on disk. Enables Librarian auto-sync

args.name: title
args.help: Title (will be slugified into id). If omitted, first line of body

args.name: workspace
args.help: Convenience: scope this item to workspace ID. Maps to scope="workspace:<ws>"

subcommands.name: search
subcommands.about: Search across mem_items (FTS5 + hybrid scoring)

args.name: kind
args.help: Filter by kind: skill | fact | note | conversation | script | peer | preference | daily | learning | rule | summary

args.name: rerank
args.help: Run LLM rerank on top candidates (requires ANTHROPIC_API_KEY)

subcommands.name: secret
subcommands.about: Pluggable secret store: save / get / search / list / delete. Backend is selected in Settings (default: bitwarden once shipped; `mock` in Phase 1 builds)

subcommands.name: delete
subcommands.about: Delete by name

subcommands.name: get
subcommands.about: Resolve and print a secret. Default = raw value to stdout (no trailing newline). Use --json for {name, value, notes}

subcommands.name: list
subcommands.about: List saved secrets (metadata only — never values)

subcommands.name: lock
subcommands.about: Lock the active backend (in-process session is dropped)

subcommands.name: logout
subcommands.about: Sign out — also drops persisted creds (OS keychain entry)

subcommands.name: save
subcommands.about: Save a secret. Value comes from --value or stdin (preferred — keeps the value out of shell history)

args.name: overwrite
args.help: Allow replacing an existing secret with the same name

args.name: value
args.help: Plaintext value. Omit and pipe via stdin instead

subcommands.name: save-master-password
subcommands.about: Save the master password to ~/.codeterm/secrets/bitwarden-master.env (mode 0600). Daemon then auto-unlocks JIT on every operation — no further prompts. Reads value from stdin (preferred — out of shell history) or --password

subcommands.name: search
subcommands.about: Free-text search over saved secret metadata

subcommands.name: status
subcommands.about: Show backend + auth status

subcommands.name: sync
subcommands.about: Pull latest from the remote vault. No-op for backends with no remote (Local OS-keychain, Mock). Bitwarden runs `bw sync`

subcommands.name: unlock
subcommands.about: Unlock the active backend with a master password (read from stdin if --password is omitted, never from argv)

subcommands.name: skill
subcommands.about: Skill management — folder-on-disk skills with mem index. Skills live as ~/.codeterm/skills/<name>/SKILL.md (+ optional support files). `add` registers the folder; Librarian re-vectorizes if SKILL.md changes

subcommands.name: add
subcommands.about: Register an existing skill folder. Reads <folder>/SKILL.md and saves a mem item with source_path linked to it. Re-runs are idempotent. Area can come from --area flag, YAML frontmatter (`area: foo`), or the parent folder name (~/.codeterm/skills/<area>/<skill>/SKILL.md)

subcommands.name: list
subcommands.about: List all registered skills

subcommands.name: new
subcommands.about: Scaffold a new skill folder under ~/.codeterm/skills/<name>/, write a SKILL.md template (with frontmatter + canonical sections) plus an empty scripts/ subdir, then register it in mem immediately. After this, edit the SKILL.md — Librarian will re-index on change

args.name: area
args.help: Optional area tag to put in the frontmatter

args.name: name
args.help: Skill slug (also folder name). Use kebab-case

subcommands.name: stats
subcommands.about: Show mem store stats (counts by kind, blob sizes)

subcommands.name: sync
subcommands.about: Trigger file sync for source-tracked items (Librarian)

subcommands.name: tail
subcommands.about: Show recent mem writes (newest first). With --follow, poll for new rows

args.name: follow
args.help: Follow mode: poll every 500ms and print new rows as they appear

subcommands.name: taxonomy
subcommands.about: Print {area -> {kind -> count}} for the store (or a single workspace)

subcommands.name: unpin
subcommands.about: Unpin a previously pinned item

subcommands.name: update
subcommands.about: Partial update of an existing mem item by id. Only the flags you pass are written; everything else stays as-is

args.name: changed_by
args.help: Actor label for audit trail (defaults to "user"). Used by automated workflows

subcommands.name: wake-up
subcommands.about: Print L0+L1 wake-up context (GA init injection)

args.name: explain
args.help: Append a per-item L1 score breakdown for debugging selection

args.name: workspace
args.help: Current workspace id — boosts pinned-in-workspace items in L1

subcommands.name: worker
subcommands.about: Graph-worker operations (hidden mem panel agents)

subcommands.name: get
subcommands.about: Get one worker by id

subcommands.name: kill
subcommands.about: Kill a worker by id

subcommands.name: list
subcommands.about: List all graph workers

subcommands.name: progress
subcommands.about: Report progress (called by worker itself; uses $CODETERM_WORKER_ID)

subcommands.name: report
subcommands.about: Submit final report and mark done (uses $CODETERM_WORKER_ID)

subcommands.name: spawn
subcommands.about: Spawn a new graph worker

subcommands.name: mesh
subcommands.about: Mesh networking — peer discovery, pairing, relay

subcommands.name: announce
subcommands.about: Push our current address list to paired peers without re-detecting locally. Use --to to limit to one peer

args.name: to
args.help: Optional target peer (instance_id or name). Omit for all peers

subcommands.name: approve
subcommands.about: Accept an incoming pairing request

args.name: request_id
args.help: Request ID of the pending pairing request

subcommands.name: broadcast
subcommands.about: Start broadcasting for the configured duration

subcommands.name: connect
subcommands.about: Initiate pairing with a discovered peer

args.name: instance_id
args.help: Instance ID or name of the discovered peer

subcommands.name: disconnect
subcommands.about: Disconnect (unpair) from a paired peer

args.name: instance_id
args.help: Instance ID of the paired peer

subcommands.name: discover
subcommands.about: Trigger mesh discovery scan (list discovered peers)

subcommands.name: exec
subcommands.about: Execute a command on a remote mesh peer

args.name: pane
args.help: Target pane on remote instance (default: general)

args.name: target
args.help: Target peer name or instance ID

subcommands.name: offline
subcommands.about: Go offline: stop pinging peers, stop announcing, stop refreshing local addresses (which keeps Tailscale alive). The daemon stays up; peers will time out our presence on their side. Local-only command

subcommands.name: online
subcommands.about: Come back online — resume mesh activity. Local-only

subcommands.name: output
subcommands.about: Get output from a pane on a remote mesh peer

args.name: pane
args.help: Target pane on remote instance (default: general)

args.name: target
args.help: Target peer name or instance ID

subcommands.name: panes
subcommands.about: List panes on a remote mesh peer

args.name: target
args.help: Target peer name or instance ID

subcommands.name: peer
subcommands.about: Per-peer address management

subcommands.name: set-addr
subcommands.about: Manually override our cached address for a paired peer. Useful when auto-detection is wrong or you want to point at a specific interface. Format: ip[:port]. Examples: codeterm mesh peer set-addr BLACKSTAR 100.64.10.1 codeterm mesh peer set-addr BLACKSTAR 192.168.1.42:7685

subcommands.name: peers
subcommands.about: List all peers (paired + discovered)

subcommands.name: refresh
subcommands.about: Re-detect local addresses (Tailscale + LAN) and announce them to all paired peers. Use after a network swap so peers update their cache without restarting CodeTerm

subcommands.name: reject
subcommands.about: Reject and block an incoming pairing request

args.name: request_id
args.help: Request ID of the pending pairing request

subcommands.name: status
subcommands.about: Show mesh status (identity, discovery, peers)

subcommands.name: stop-broadcast
subcommands.about: Stop broadcasting immediately

subcommands.name: notifications
subcommands.about: List or manage notifications

subcommands.name: clear
subcommands.about: Clear all notifications

subcommands.name: notify
subcommands.about: Send a notification

subcommands.name: pane
subcommands.about: Pane management

subcommands.name: chat
subcommands.about: Read a pane's parsed chat transcript (text/thinking/tool calls/results)

args.name: pane
args.help: Target pane ID (default: $CODETERM_PANE_ID or focused pane)

args.name: since
args.help: Only return messages from this index onward

subcommands.name: close
subcommands.about: Close a pane by ID

subcommands.name: current

subcommands.name: resume
subcommands.about: Resume a past session in its original cwd. Atomic replacement for the "workspace create → agent spawn --args=--resume=UUID" dance which keeps failing because Claude/Codex look for the JSONL in the current cwd. This command: finds the session across providers, creates a workspace at the right project path, spawns an agent pane there, and hands the resume id to the provider correctly

subcommands.name: system
subcommands.about: OS-level integration: autostart, supervision, install hooks. Each subcommand is local-only and writes to platform-specific places (schtasks on Windows, LaunchAgents on macOS, user systemd on Linux)

subcommands.name: autostart-status
subcommands.about: Print whether the autostart trigger is installed and where

subcommands.name: disable-autostart
subcommands.about: Remove the OS-level autostart trigger created by `enable-autostart`. Idempotent — running on a host without a trigger is a no-op

subcommands.name: enable-autostart
subcommands.about: Install an OS-level trigger that auto-launches CodeTerm at user login and re-launches it if the process disappears. Per platform: Windows = `schtasks` task with ONLOGON + 5-minute repeat, macOS = `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.codeterm.app.plist` with `KeepAlive` + `RunAtLoad`, Linux = user systemd unit `~/.config/systemd/user/codeterm.service` with `Restart=on-failure`. Idempotent — running twice is a no-op

args.name: binary
args.help: Override the path to the CodeTerm executable. Defaults to the installed app binary for the current platform
